children: ) is planning its second yen-denominated bond offering since Warren Buffett stepped down as chief executive officer, reports Bloomberg.

The company has been issuing yen-denominated bonds at a pace of twice a year. In April, it sold six tranches with maturities ranging from three to 30 years, raising a total of ¥272.3 billion ($1.7 billion). The offering was among Berkshire’s largest yen bond sales, behind only its debut issuance in 2019 and its October 2024 sale.

The latest offering comes as Japanese companies have slowed domestic bond sales, while spreads in the country's domestic corporate bond market have widened from 45.67 basis points in May to 52.37 bps in November.

Berkshire has mandated Mizuho Securities and BofA Securities for a potential benchmark yen bond offering, which is expected in the near future, subject to market conditions, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: Berkshire plans second yen-denominated bond offering of 2026
